assumptions: Three billing windows, one owner and one transport, with idempotent per-kind settlement. Safety does not assume provider success or eventual settlement. Conditional progress uses the explicit fair-completion assumptions below.

A stopped renewal returns without granting its window. Failed credit settlement retains that window for idempotent retry. An additive quota refund with unknown acknowledgement is retained without replay; confirmed independent money remains separate.
A settled window abstracts matching terminal receipts; an ungranted window requires actual zero receipts. Missing, nonzero or mismatched receipts are failed settlement and retain ownership.
bounds.progress: After Stop, confirmation follows only if pending admission/refusal and stopped-renewal work returns, each funded window obtains its terminal settlement receipt, quota release returns a known or unknown result, and confirmation runs. Weak fairness expresses these assumptions; it does not promise provider availability, settlement success, transport closure or a wall-clock deadline. Confirmation requires independently terminal money. An unknown quota-refund acknowledgement stays unknown; this property does not imply a successful refund or successful overall cleanup.

limitations: Three-window safety abstraction. Controlled real-relay tests replay Stop during quota, admission and extension waits, zero-settlement failure/retry, and one-shot quota uncertainty. The model aggregates per-kind credit receipts by window and does not establish physical provider closure, timing, browser, native client or live-provider qualification.
Conditional progress applies to the modeled idempotent per-kind receipt path. A failed generic immutable settlement remains unconfirmed; no successful retry is promised for that legacy contract.

The separate LemmaScript proof covers usage-share bounds and conservation for finite safe integer counters with safe index multiplication. It does not prove asynchronous lifecycle behavior or caller compliance with those arithmetic assumptions.

The production Cloud caller limits sessions to 1–120 windows and applies server-owned stream budgets. Generic host consumers must satisfy the helper’s safe-integer and multiplication preconditions for this arithmetic proof; no new runtime cap is imposed.

assumptions: Weak fairness of admission/refusal completion, stopped-renewal completion, each funded window terminal settlement, quota-result completion and confirmation.

Terminal settlement availability is assumed for conditional progress only; provider closure and wall-clock completion are outside this model. Quota acknowledgement may remain unknown and is never replayed.
The quota outcome may be permanently unknown. No transition resolves or retries it; independently terminal money allows confirmation while preserving that unknown field.
No fairness or external completion is assumed. Stop may retain an unresolved admission or unacknowledged settlement indefinitely.
